lines.say: Why do your ears pop on a plane?
lines.caption: Ears pop
lines.cap: Why do your ears pop on a plane?

lines.say: As the plane climbs, the air in the cabin thins out, like on a mountain.
lines.caption: Thin air
lines.cap: As the plane climbs, the air in the cabin thins out, like on a mountain.

lines.say: But behind your eardrum sits a pocket of air still at ground pressure.
lines.caption: Air pocket
lines.cap: But behind your eardrum sits a pocket of air still at ground pressure.

lines.say: It pushes the eardrum out, and sounds go muffled.
lines.caption: Bulge
lines.cap: It pushes the eardrum out, and sounds go muffled.

lines.say: A thin tube links that pocket to your throat. Swallow or yawn, and it opens.
lines.caption: The tube
lines.cap: A thin tube links that pocket to your throat. Swallow or yawn, and it opens.

lines.say: Air rushes through, the pressure evens out, and pop!
lines.caption: Pop
lines.cap: Air rushes through, the pressure evens out, and POP!

lines.say: That's why chewing gum helps. More swallowing, more pops.
lines.caption: Gum
lines.cap: That's why chewing gum helps. More swallowing, more pops.
